item.title: UAV-Based Federated Learning Incentive Mechanism for Latency-Aware Multimodal Target Tracking
item.description: Federated multimodal learning (FML) over uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) networks underpins privacy-preserving multimodal target tracking, yet energy-constrained and self-interested UAVs, which bear substantial sensing, training, and transmission costs, are reluctant to continuously contribute the high-quality multimodal data on which the global tracking model depends. To address this issue, this research aims to design an incentive mechanism that maximizes the aggregate FML efficiency and ensures economic fairness. This article proposes a novel two-stage incentive framework for UAV-assisted FML networks, modeled as a two-sided market between ground task requesters (TRs) and modality-specific UAVs. A TR purchases inference access to the updated multimodal target tracking model enabled by one UAV’s FML service. In the first stage, we develop a joint latency-modality-aware initial matching (JLMA-IM) algorithm. By constructing an FML-efficiency index that integrates physical-layer latency with modality importance, we cast the assignment as an aggregate-efficiency maximization problem and solve it exactly via a weighted bipartite matching approach. In the second stage, we design a double auction-based winner and pricing determination (DA-WPD) algorithm based on candidate critical pairs to determine final winners and transaction prices. We theoretically prove that the proposed mechanism satisfies individual rationality and budget balance, and that it is truthful under a boundary-stability condition. Simulation results show that the market-driven federated training achieves tracking accuracy comparable to full participation on 114 visible-thermal uncrewed aerial vehicle (VTUAV) sequences, JLMA-IM improves the FML efficiency by approximately 15% and reduces the bottleneck latency by up to 25%, and DA-WPD completes more transactions with higher social welfare than the McAfee double auction.
